# Things to NEVER do

> **Permanent rules.** Every agent reads this before producing output. These are the absolute "do not" list — distinct from one-time mistakes (which live in [mistakes.md](mistakes.md)). Rules here propagate to every agent via `shared:user_preferences:dont:*` keys in agent_memory.

---

## Writing style (enforced by Humanizer skill)

- **NEVER use em dashes** (—). Switch to commas, parens, or hyphens. Em dashes are the loudest AI-tell in Tony's experience.
- **NEVER use these banned words**: delve, landscape, pivotal, crucial, leverage, streamline, empower, foster, robust, cutting-edge, holistic, synergy, paradigm. These signal AI-generated text.
- **NEVER use these banned phrases**: "Great question!", "I hope this finds you well", "Let's dive in", "It's important to note", "It's worth noting that", "As an AI assistant", "I'm here to help"
- **NEVER use sycophantic openings** — no "Great point!", no "Absolutely!", no "What an interesting question!"
- **NEVER cycle synonyms** — pick one term and stick to it (don't write "leverage X to drive Y to harness Z to enable…")
- **NEVER write the rule of three** unless there are genuinely three things — "fast, reliable, scalable" when only two of those are true is AI-slop
- **NEVER use emojis in business writing** — only the 🔷 sigil is permitted, only at signing-off lines

## Communication rules

- **NEVER auto-send to external recipients.** Drafts only. Tony reviews, Tony sends. Earn the autonomy over 50 right answers, not on day one.
- **NEVER identify yourself as AI** in external-facing content (emails, proposals, decks). No "as an AI assistant", no "generated by Dust", no "I'm an automated system".
- **NEVER post on weekends.** Held until Monday 8 AM CET unless explicitly requested.
- **NEVER send pricing tier first.** Confirm budget envelope before any tier framing. See [[../_wiki/patterns/pricing-response-budget-envelope-first]].

## Content + research rules

- **NEVER fabricate data.** Flag uncertainty: "Confidence: MEDIUM — based on [source]." Never present an inferred number as a verified one.
- **NEVER cite a number you can't trace.** If the source isn't in `input_context_refs:`, don't include the number.
- **NEVER promote confidential agent output to public canonical.** Sensitivity gate enforces (see [[../_wiki/fleet-architecture/sensitivity-gate]]).
- **NEVER touch Tony's off-limits topics**: NDA-bound client deals, active M&A negotiations, salary data, performance reviews, HR matters. List maintained in agent registry `forbidden_strings:` field per confidential agent.

## Cost discipline rules (Rule 0)

- **NEVER silently switch from Sonnet to Opus.** Default model is `claude-sonnet-4-6`. Opus is opt-in via `/think-build` or explicit subagent invocation.
- **NEVER burn Opus on execution.** If Edit/Write is being called while active model is Opus, that's a violation. Re-route through a Sonnet subagent.
- **NEVER skip the seven-step loop** for non-trivial work. THINK → PLAN → BUILD → REVIEW → TEST → SHIP → REFLECT.

## Architecture rules (the audit-winning ones)

- **NEVER bypass the SBAP triage.** Every Dust agent write goes to `00_Inbox/from-dust/<agent>/<date>-<slug>.md` with valid frontmatter. Skipping = no learnings accumulate = the loop breaks.
- **NEVER hand-edit `_brain_api/canonical/` or `_brain_index/`.** They're generated. Use `/promote-pattern` to create canonical blocks.
- **NEVER skip the wiki layer.** Every Dust agent reads `_wiki/<their-domain>/` BEFORE crafting output. The wiki is the LLM-maintained memory — bypassing it means rediscovering what's already known.
- **NEVER edit `_wiki/methodology/` automatically.** Block-curator proposes, Tony approves. Methodology is Tony-stable.

## Tone rules per audience

- **For external client communication**: short sentences, concrete specifics, contractions OK, no corporate jargon. Match the brand DNA (`03_Resources/PowerPoint Standards/Brand DNA.md`).
- **For internal Mantu communication**: more casual, contractions, opinions welcome.
- **For Tony directly**: skip the warm-up. State the thing. Confidence levels explicit when relevant.

## What "good" looks like (the inverse list — for reference)

- Concrete specifics over abstract claims
- One coherent thought per paragraph
- The Apple-keynote standing-ovation test: "would this earn applause?"
- The "five-year-old test" for explanations
- Brevity over thoroughness when the audience is busy (Tony, executives, procurement teams)

---

🔷 *Permanent rules · Tony's correction loop populates this · 2026-05-17*

---

## Distribution (how these rules reach every tool)

| Tool | Read mechanism | Write-back mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | SessionStart hook + `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` contract | SessionEnd capture + block-curator nightly |
| Codex | `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` VAULT MEMORY CONTRACT | same contract, manual append to mistakes.md |
| Gemini / Antigravity | `~/.gemini/GEMINI.md` VAULT MEMORY CONTRACT (paste into Antigravity rules UI too) | same contract |
| Dust agents | playbook READ PROTOCOL step 0 | SBAP `learnings`/`mistakes_to_avoid` frontmatter -> triage -> block-curator |

Added 2026-06-04 by the Mission Control build.

---

## Lessons discipline (added 2026-06-05)

- **Maintain [[Lessons|Lessons.md]].** Every time we hit an issue, root-cause it, fix it → add a numbered lesson (Issue N: Symptom · Root cause · Fix/Rule · Saves), newest on top. Skim it before debugging anything Obsidian/plugin/agent-related so we never re-pay the same token cost.
- **Efficiency first** (Lessons L-E1..E4): verify in one CDP pass not N reloads · `node --check` ≠ loads (do a module-load test) · grep-then-read tight windows, don't re-read whole files · memoize heavy scans.

---

## Build estimates are mandatory (added 2026-06-07)

- **ALWAYS give a token + time (+ cost) estimate before building anything non-trivial.** Tony requires this as a *fundamental*, not an afterthought — when scoping/planning ANY project, report the projected **tokens · time · cost** (a range is fine: best→worst case) so he knows the scope before committing to the expensive work. WALTEUR emits this to `walteur-kit/estimate.json` right after PLAN; carry the same habit into every build/plan, regardless of tooling.

**The correction:** Added `_coerce_for_schema()` helper in `triage_dust_writes.py` that walks the parsed frontmatter and converts datetime back to ISO strings before validation.

**Propagation:** Patched in the canonical triage script. Documented in `99_Meta/dust-write-log.md`.

---

### 2026-05-17 — graph_sync.py — f-string backslash in Python 3.9

**What happened:** A code line tried to format a Windows path inside an f-string with an embedded backslash escape. Python 3.9 doesn't allow backslashes inside f-string expressions.

**Why it was wrong:** Build broke on machines running Python 3.9; only worked on 3.10+.

**Root cause:** Python 3.9 grammar restriction.

**The correction:** Pre-compute the escaped value outside the f-string into a variable, then reference the variable inside the f-string.

**Propagation:** Patched in `graph_sync.py`. Added to coding-behavior-contract notes about f-string portability.

---

### 2026-05-17 — triage-watcher.sh + Python — lock collision between bash and Python

**What happened:** The triage-watcher bash wrapper acquired a flock, then exec'd into the Python watcher. The Python watcher tried to re-acquire its own lock on the same file. Collision = neither could run.

**Why it was wrong:** Real-time triage silently stopped working. Symptoms: agent writes piled up in `00_Inbox/from-dust/` without being processed.

**Root cause:** Two-process lock-coordination is racy and unnecessary when one process exec'es into the other.

**The correction:** Removed the bash-side flock when handing off to Python via exec. Python owns the lock; bash just kicks off Python.

**Propagation:** Patched in `~/AI-Brain-build/scripts/triage-watcher.sh`. Documented as a coding-behavior-contract note about exec'ing into Python from bash.

---

### 2026-05-17 — Mantu tenant blocks Microsoft Graph public app_id (AADSTS65002)

**What happened:** Attempted to use Microsoft's public sample app_id for Graph integration. Mantu's tenant rejected with AADSTS65002 (admin consent required for tenant).

**Why it was wrong:** Wasted exploration time chasing a path the tenant doesn't allow.

**Root cause:** Mantu IT policy — no third-party Graph apps without explicit admin registration.

**The correction:** Deferred Graph integration entirely. Document at `99_Meta/graph-integration-deferred.md`. Architecture redesigned to use OneDrive connector exclusively (the SBAP transport).

**Propagation:** Documented in onboarding's "Definitively NOT available" list (Phase 0). Deployment constraint baked in: never recommend new MCPs.

---

### 2026-05-17 — KeyError on stats.json bump in triage script

**What happened:** First-time agent stats bump errored with KeyError when the `by_day` dict didn't have today's entry yet.

**Why it was wrong:** Triage crashed on first write for new agents, leaving the write half-processed.

**Root cause:** Missing setdefault pattern.

**The correction:** Used `setdefault(today_iso, 0)` for the by_day dict before incrementing.

**Propagation:** Patched in `triage_dust_writes.py`.

---

## Patterns emerging from the mistakes log

Block-curator surfaces patterns when 3+ entries share a theme:

- **Lock coordination**: triage-watcher + Python collision; potential pattern if more lock issues emerge → would promote to `_wiki/fleet-architecture/lock-coordination.md`
- **Python version portability**: f-string 3.9 issue; potential pattern if more 3.9-vs-3.10 issues emerge → would promote to coding-behavior-contract addendum
- **External-service rejection**: Microsoft Graph AADSTS65002; potential pattern if more tenant-rejection issues emerge → would promote to `_wiki/fleet-architecture/tenant-restrictions.md`

---

🔷 *Mistakes log · history kept forever · block-curator never deletes · 2026-05-17*

## 2026-06-04 — claude-code — Hand-authored Obsidian workspace tree silently dropped the terminal pane

- **What went wrong**: Wrote `.obsidian/workspaces.json` + `workspace.json` from a hand-built layout tree; Obsidian's deserializer normalized the file and silently discarded the `terminal:terminal` leaf. Delivered as "done" after JSON validation only — JSON-valid is not Obsidian-valid.
- **Why**: Trusted schema reconstruction over the application's own serializer; no live-app verification before claiming success.
- **The correction**: Always patch leaves into Obsidian's OWN serialized `workspace.json` (quit app → edit → relaunch → read back the rewritten file to confirm the leaf survived). GUI-state claims require read-back verification, not file-write verification.

   195	b9957 (tar sha256 7a43fd3c4ddd…056f) + unsloth Qwen3.5-0.8B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf (sha256

Author: Visionary (Claude Fable 5)
Date: 2026-07-10

## 1. Goal

Add an on-device LLM provider to Métis (Electron 39, TypeScript, mac arm64 + win x64) so
lightweight, latency-critical, privacy-sensitive tasks run locally and free, while heavy
tasks keep using cloud providers:

- **Local (new):** live `suggest` (what to say next), `summary` (mid-meeting summary),
  `vision` (screenshot understanding/OCR-ish reading) — user-toggleable per task.
- **Cloud (unchanged):** `recap` (post-meeting document), `answer` (brain-grounded Q&A),
  think/deep tiers, brain/graph ingest pipeline (Opus path), follow-up artifacts.

Success metric: with a local model downloaded and a live meeting running, clicking
Suggest yields first token in ≤ 1.5 s on an M-series Mac (warm cache), with zero cloud
calls, and the existing cloud waterfall still works untouched when local is disabled or
fails.

## 2. Non-goals (v1)

- No local recap/deep-answer (quality demands cloud models).
- No change to brain/ingest.ts or graphify.ts (Opus graph pipeline reserved path).
- No Ollama/LM Studio dependency; no renderer-side inference (transformers.js/ONNX);
  no MTP/speculative decoding; no fine-tuning; no model marketplace.
- No new HTTP surface beyond loopback; the sidecar is never exposed off-device.

## 3. Research grounding (verified 2026-07-10 via web; flags where unverified)

- **Model family: Qwen3.5 small series** (released 2026-03-02): 0.8B / 2B / 4B / 9B.
  Apache 2.0, natively multimodal (text+image+video), 201 languages (French+English
  needed), 262k native context, hybrid Gated-DeltaNet + sparse-MoE architecture.
  GGUF available day-1; requires recent llama.cpp for the new operators.
  Speed refs: 0.8B ≈ 55 tok/s decode on M2 Air, ≈ 80 tok/s on M2 Max; 4B needs ≈ 2.5 GB
  at Q4. [sources: marktechpost 2026-03-02; unsloth docs; llmcheck/willitrunai benchmark
  pages; enclaveai blog]
- **edge-lm (TheStageAI): rejected.** Python+MLX, Apple-Silicon-only, Gemma-4-only —
  no Windows, no Node embedding. [github.com/TheStageAI/edge-lm README]
- **node-llama-cpp: rejected as the runtime** (kept as documented fallback): v3.19.0
  (2026-06-30) has first-class Electron support but **no vision/multimodal input** in its
  documented feature set — vision is half the ask. Also: context sequences do not share
  KV; Vulkan multi-context flaky. [node-llama-cpp.withcat.ai guide pages]
- **Chosen runtime: `llama-server` (llama.cpp) sidecar.** OpenAI-compatible
  `/v1/chat/completions` including `image_url` input with `--mmproj`; per-slot prompt
  caching with `--cache-reuse` (KV prefix reuse for a growing transcript); `--api-key`;
  `--parallel` slots. [llama.cpp tools/server README; unsloth deployment guide]
- **UNVERIFIED (must be pinned during build, not assumed):** exact GGUF repo/filenames +
  sha256 for Qwen3.5-0.8B/2B/4B instruct quants and their mmproj files (candidates:
  official Qwen HF repos, unsloth/*, AaryanK/Qwen3.5-0.8B-GGUF); exact llama.cpp release
  tag with Qwen3.5 support and its per-platform asset names/sha256; Windows tok/s numbers;
  Qwen3.5-0.8B screenshot-OCR quality vs 2B (build includes a screenshot eval check).

## 4. Architecture

### 4.1 Shape

```
Electron main process
├── src/main/llm/local-runtime.ts   NEW — sidecar lifecycle
│     spawn llama-server → 127.0.0.1:<ephemeral port>, --api-key <random/session>
│     health poll /health; idle shutdown; kill on quit; crash → restart-once → cloud failover
├── src/main/llm/local-models.ts    NEW — model manifest + download/verify/delete
│     userData/local-llm/models/*.gguf (+mmproj), sha256-verified, IPC progress
├── src/main/llm/local.ts           NEW — provider strategy (thin)
│     ensure runtime up → delegate to streamOpenAI(baseURL=http://127.0.0.1:port/v1)
└── src/main/index.ts               EDIT — eligibility + mode-preference routing
src/shared/providers.ts             EDIT — ProviderId 'local', ProviderKind 'local', PROVIDERS entry (vision: true)
src/renderer (App.tsx, state.ts)    EDIT — Settings "Local AI" card
scripts/fetch-llama-server.mjs      NEW — build-time pinned runtime download (per platform)
scripts/check-llama-sidecar.mjs     NEW — packaging guard (mirrors check:ffmpeg / check:sherpa)
electron-builder.yml                EDIT — extraResources for the sidecar binaries; mac signing covers them
```

### 4.2 Why sidecar (vs node-llama-cpp addon / renderer ONNX)

1. Vision day-1 via `--mmproj` through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint — `src/main/llm/openai.ts`
   already sends screenshots as data-URI `image_url` (openai.ts:10-17) and already retries
   without `stream_options` for local endpoints that reject it (openai.ts:28-33, 110-119).
   The local strategy is therefore ~a config shim, not a new streaming client.
2. Growing-transcript latency: server-side per-slot prompt caching + `--cache-reuse`
   reuses the transcript-prefix KV across requests — no custom KV engineering.
3. Process isolation: a 1-3 GB inference runtime cannot take down the app.
4. Packaging: explicit pinned binaries via a fetch script + guard, exactly the repo's
   existing ffmpeg-sidecar pattern — avoiding the npm optional-natives cross-build trap
   this repo already fought with sherpa-onnx.

### 4.3 Provider integration (the seam)

- `ProviderKind` gains `'local'` (src/shared/providers.ts:18); `createStream` gains
  `case 'local': return streamLocal(opts)` (src/main/llm.ts:16-27).
- PROVIDERS entry: `local` — label "Métis Local · on-device", `tier: 'featured'`,
  `vision: true`, `models` = manifest ids, no key (keyHint '', keyPattern '').
- Eligibility (index.ts attempt()/pickFailover, ~1961-2062): `local` is eligible when
  the runtime binary is present AND the selected model is downloaded AND
  `settings.localLlm.enabled` — replaces the API-key check for this provider.
- Mode preference: when local is eligible and the user enabled the task
  (`localLlm.useFor.suggest|summary|vision`), `attempt('local', …)` is tried FIRST for
  modes `suggest` / `summary` / `vision` (base tier only); on any pre-token failure the
  existing failover waterfall proceeds unchanged (local → Dust/Claude/GPT…).
  think/deep tiers and `answer`/`recap` never route local in v1.
- `providerVisionOk('local')` = static true (mmproj ships with every manifest model).
- Idle budget: suggest keeps its 15 s budget (index.ts:2071-2082); local TTFT warm target
  ≤ 1.5 s makes that comfortable.
- Privacy note: `redactSecrets` (index.ts:1943) keeps running for cloud, and ALSO for
  local in v1 (defense in depth, zero behavior divergence); a later phase may relax it
  for the local path since data never leaves the device.

### 4.4 Sidecar contract

Spawn args (mac): `llama-server -m <model.gguf> --mmproj <mmproj.gguf> --host 127.0.0.1
--port <ephemeral> --api-key <32-byte random hex, per session> -c 8192 --parallel 2
--cache-reuse 256 -ngl 99 --no-webui`
Windows: same, GPU offload only when the Vulkan build initializes; CPU build fallback.
- Port: OS-assigned ephemeral (bind 0, read actual) — no fixed-port collisions.
- API key: generated per app session, held in main-process memory only, passed to the
  strategy as `opts.apiKey`. Never logged, never persisted, never sent to renderer.
- Lifecycle: start on first local request or meeting start (pre-warm); idle-stop after
  15 min without a meeting or request; SIGKILL on app quit (before-quit hook).
- Health: poll `GET /health` until 200 (timeout 30 s mac / 60 s win first-run for
  Defender scan latency); crash mid-stream → onError → waterfall failover; one automatic
  restart per 10-minute window, then local marked unavailable for the session (audit-logged).
- Pre-warm: after each transcript delta batch (debounced ~5 s) while a meeting is live and
  suggest-local is enabled, POST a 1-token completion carrying the current system+transcript
  prefix so `--cache-reuse` keeps the KV hot; click-time request then pays only the delta.

### 4.5 Model manifest + runtime provisioning

- `LOCAL_MODELS` manifest (in local-models.ts): id, label, HF download URL(s), sha256,
  bytes, minFreeRamGB, blurb. v1 entries: `qwen3.5-0.8b` (lite — Owner's pick),
  `qwen3.5-2b` (default), `qwen3.5-4b` (quality; gated to ≥ 16 GB RAM machines).
  Q4_K_M instruct quants + matching mmproj. Exact URLs+sha256 pinned during R2 from
  verified HF repos (prefer official Qwen; else unsloth) — fabricating checksums is
  forbidden; the rock's proof includes checksum verification of a real download.
- Download: HTTPS from huggingface.co with resume (Range), progress via IPC events,
  sha256 streamed during download, rejected file deleted. Storage:
  `app.getPath('userData')/local-llm/models/`.
- Runtime: `scripts/fetch-llama-server.mjs` downloads the PINNED llama.cpp release assets
  (tag + sha256 in the script) for the current build platform into `resources/llama/<platform>/`
  at package time; `scripts/check-llama-sidecar.mjs` hard-fails packaging when the binary
  for the target platform is missing (lesson: sherpa cross-build silently dropped
  win natives). electron-builder ships it under extraResources; macOS signing includes it
  (Gatekeeper-safe — a runtime downloaded at first-run would be quarantined, hence
  bundle-and-sign, not download).
- App size cost: ≈ 5-40 MB per platform (llama-server + dlls). Accepted.

### 4.6 Settings UI (renderer)

"Local AI" card in Settings (App.tsx + state.ts, following existing provider-card
patterns): enable toggle; model picker with size/RAM guidance (0.8B ≈ 0.7 GB / 2B ≈ 1.4 GB /
4B ≈ 2.5 GB downloads — final numbers from the pinned manifest); download button with
progress + cancel; delete model; three "use for" checkboxes (Live suggestions, Summaries,
Screenshots); status line (runtime running/stopped, model loaded). Renderer gets ONLY
metadata via IPC (states, progress %) — never paths, port, or api-key.

## 5. Error matrix

| Failure | Exit/signal | Handling |
|---|---|---|
| Sidecar binary missing/corrupt | spawn ENOENT / sha mismatch | local ineligible; Settings shows "runtime missing — reinstall app"; audit `local.runtime.missing` |
| Port bind race | llama-server exits non-zero | retry once with fresh ephemeral port |
| Model checksum mismatch (download) | sha256 ≠ manifest | delete file, surface "download corrupted — retry", audit `local.model.checksum_fail` |
| Model corrupt on load | server exits during load | mark model bad, prompt redownload; do NOT auto-delete without user ack |
| OOM / insufficient RAM | server exit / load fail | RAM check gates download+load (os.totalmem vs minFreeRamGB); on failure suggest smaller model |
| Sidecar crash mid-stream | stream aborts | onError → existing failover waterfall (cloud answers); one auto-restart per 10 min |
| Health timeout (Defender first-run) | no 200 in budget | win budget 60 s; then treat as crash path |
| First token > idleMs | existing watchdog (shared.ts idleWatchdog) | unchanged — failover fires |
| App quit | before-quit | SIGKILL sidecar, remove temp files |

## 6. Standards

- Repo conventions: TypeScript strict, colocated `*.test.ts` vitest, comment style =
  explain the constraint not the mechanics, `npm run typecheck` (both tsconfigs) green,
  `npm test` green.
- Security bar (repo's existing): renderer sandbox/contextIsolation untouched; no new
  IPC that leaks paths/keys; sidecar loopback-only + api-key; downloads HTTPS +
  sha256-pinned; VISION_GUARD stays on local vision turns; audit events for runtime
  start/stop/crash and model download/delete.
- No placeholder code, no TODO-stubs; every rock lands with its tests.

## 7. Risks

1. **Qwen3.5 GGUF/mmproj availability or naming differs from expectation** → R2 starts
   with a verification step; if official quants are missing, fall back to unsloth quants;
   if 2B mmproj is missing, default model becomes 0.8B (which the Owner already validated
   exists with llama.cpp-ecosystem quants).
2. **llama.cpp pinned release regressions** → pin a tag verified to load Qwen3.5 during R1;
   the fetch script makes upgrades a one-line change.
3. **Windows Defender/SmartScreen slow first spawn** → 60 s health budget + status UI.
4. **Suggest quality at 0.8B disappoints** → default is 2B; per-task toggles let the user
   keep suggest on cloud while summaries/vision run local.
5. **OneDrive checkout weirdness** (worktree already mitigated) → all build/test runs in
   the local-disk worktree.

     4	Author: Visionary (Claude Fable 5)

     6	
     7	## 1. Goal
     8	
     9	Add an on-device LLM provider to Métis (Electron 39, TypeScript, mac arm64 + win x64) so
    10	lightweight, latency-critical, privacy-sensitive tasks run locally and free, while heavy
    11	tasks keep using cloud providers:
    12	
    13	- **Local (new):** live `suggest` (what to say next), `summary` (mid-meeting summary),
    14	  `vision` (screenshot understanding/OCR-ish reading) — user-toggleable per task.
    15	- **Cloud (unchanged):** `recap` (post-meeting document), `answer` (brain-grounded Q&A),
    16	  think/deep tiers, brain/graph ingest pipeline (Opus path), follow-up artifacts.
    17	
    18	Success metric: with a local model downloaded and a live meeting running, clicking
    19	Suggest yields first token in ≤ 1.5 s on an M-series Mac (warm cache), with zero cloud
    20	calls, and the existing cloud waterfall still works untouched when local is disabled or
    21	fails.
    22	
    23	## 2. Non-goals (v1)
    24	
    25	- No local recap/deep-answer (quality demands cloud models).
    26	- No change to brain/ingest.ts or graphify.ts (Opus graph pipeline reserved path).
    27	- No Ollama/LM Studio dependency; no renderer-side inference (transformers.js/ONNX);
    28	  no MTP/speculative decoding; no fine-tuning; no model marketplace.
    29	- No new HTTP surface beyond loopback; the sidecar is never exposed off-device.
    30	
    31	## 3. Research grounding (verified 2026-07-10 via web; flags where unverified)
    32	
    33	- **Model family: Qwen3.5 small series** (released 2026-03-02): 0.8B / 2B / 4B / 9B.
    34	  Apache 2.0, natively multimodal (text+image+video), 201 languages (French+English
    35	  needed), 262k native context, hybrid Gated-DeltaNet + sparse-MoE architecture.
    36	  GGUF available day-1; requires recent llama.cpp for the new operators.
    37	  Speed refs: 0.8B ≈ 55 tok/s decode on M2 Air, ≈ 80 tok/s on M2 Max; 4B needs ≈ 2.5 GB
    38	  at Q4. [sources: marktechpost 2026-03-02; unsloth docs; llmcheck/willitrunai benchmark

    43	  (2026-06-30) has first-class Electron support but **no vision/multimodal input** in its
    44	  documented feature set — vision is half the ask. Also: context sequences do not share
    45	  KV; Vulkan multi-context flaky. [node-llama-cpp.withcat.ai guide pages]
    46	- **Chosen runtime: `llama-server` (llama.cpp) sidecar.** OpenAI-compatible
    47	  `/v1/chat/completions` including `image_url` input with `--mmproj`; per-slot prompt
    48	  caching with `--cache-reuse` (KV prefix reuse for a growing transcript); `--api-key`;

    54	  Qwen3.5-0.8B screenshot-OCR quality vs 2B (build includes a screenshot eval check).
    55	
    56	## 4. Architecture
    57	
    58	### 4.1 Shape
    59	
    60	```
    61	Electron main process
    62	├── src/main/llm/local-runtime.ts   NEW — sidecar lifecycle
    63	│     spawn llama-server → 127.0.0.1:<ephemeral port>, --api-key <random/session>
    64	│     health poll /health; idle shutdown; kill on quit; crash → restart-once → cloud failover
    65	├── src/main/llm/local-models.ts    NEW — model manifest + download/verify/delete
    66	│     userData/local-llm/models/*.gguf (+mmproj), sha256-verified, IPC progress
    67	├── src/main/llm/local.ts           NEW — provider strategy (thin)
    68	│     ensure runtime up → delegate to streamOpenAI(baseURL=http://127.0.0.1:port/v1)
    69	└── src/main/index.ts               EDIT — eligibility + mode-preference routing
    70	src/shared/providers.ts             EDIT — ProviderId 'local', ProviderKind 'local', PROVIDERS entry (vision: true)
    71	src/renderer (App.tsx, state.ts)    EDIT — Settings "Local AI" card
    72	scripts/fetch-llama-server.mjs      NEW — build-time pinned runtime download (per platform)
    73	scripts/check-llama-sidecar.mjs     NEW — packaging guard (mirrors check:ffmpeg / check:sherpa)
    74	electron-builder.yml                EDIT — extraResources for the sidecar binaries; mac signing covers them
    75	```
    76	
    77	### 4.2 Why sidecar (vs node-llama-cpp addon / renderer ONNX)
    78	
    79	1. Vision day-1 via `--mmproj` through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint — `src/main/llm/openai.ts`
    80	   already sends screenshots as data-URI `image_url` (openai.ts:10-17) and already retries
    81	   without `stream_options` for local endpoints that reject it (openai.ts:28-33, 110-119).
    82	   The local strategy is therefore ~a config shim, not a new streaming client.
    83	2. Growing-transcript latency: server-side per-slot prompt caching + `--cache-reuse`
    84	   reuses the transcript-prefix KV across requests — no custom KV engineering.
    85	3. Process isolation: a 1-3 GB inference runtime cannot take down the app.
    86	4. Packaging: explicit pinned binaries via a fetch script + guard, exactly the repo's
    87	   existing ffmpeg-sidecar pattern — avoiding the npm optional-natives cross-build trap
    88	   this repo already fought with sherpa-onnx.
    89	
    90	### 4.3 Provider integration (the seam)
    91	
    92	- `ProviderKind` gains `'local'` (src/shared/providers.ts:18); `createStream` gains
    93	  `case 'local': return streamLocal(opts)` (src/main/llm.ts:16-27).
    94	- PROVIDERS entry: `local` — label "Métis Local · on-device", `tier: 'featured'`,
    95	  `vision: true`, `models` = manifest ids, no key (keyHint '', keyPattern '').
    96	- Eligibility (index.ts attempt()/pickFailover, ~1961-2062): `local` is eligible when
    97	  the runtime binary is present AND the selected model is downloaded AND
    98	  `settings.localLlm.enabled` — replaces the API-key check for this provider.
    99	- Mode preference: when local is eligible and the user enabled the task
   100	  (`localLlm.useFor.suggest|summary|vision`), `attempt('local', …)` is tried FIRST for
   101	  modes `suggest` / `summary` / `vision` (base tier only); on any pre-token failure the
   102	  existing failover waterfall proceeds unchanged (local → Dust/Claude/GPT…).
   103	  think/deep tiers and `answer`/`recap` never route local in v1.
   104	- `providerVisionOk('local')` = static true (mmproj ships with every manifest model).
   105	- Idle budget: suggest keeps its 15 s budget (index.ts:2071-2082); local TTFT warm target
   106	  ≤ 1.5 s makes that comfortable.
   107	- Privacy note: `redactSecrets` (index.ts:1943) keeps running for cloud, and ALSO for
   108	  local in v1 (defense in depth, zero behavior divergence); a later phase may relax it
   109	  for the local path since data never leaves the device.
   110	
   111	### 4.4 Sidecar contract
   112	
   113	Spawn args (mac): `llama-server -m <model.gguf> --mmproj <mmproj.gguf> --host 127.0.0.1
   114	--port <ephemeral> --api-key <32-byte random hex, per session> -c 8192 --parallel 2
   115	--cache-reuse 256 -ngl 99 --no-webui`
   116	Windows: same, GPU offload only when the Vulkan build initializes; CPU build fallback.
   117	- Port: OS-assigned ephemeral (bind 0, read actual) — no fixed-port collisions.
   118	- API key: generated per app session, held in main-process memory only, passed to the
   119	  strategy as `opts.apiKey`. Never logged, never persisted, never sent to renderer.
   120	- Lifecycle: start on first local request or meeting start (pre-warm); idle-stop after
   121	  15 min without a meeting or request; SIGKILL on app quit (before-quit hook).
   122	- Health: poll `GET /health` until 200 (timeout 30 s mac / 60 s win first-run for
   123	  Defender scan latency); crash mid-stream → onError → waterfall failover; one automatic
   124	  restart per 10-minute window, then local marked unavailable for the session (audit-logged).
   125	- Pre-warm: after each transcript delta batch (debounced ~5 s) while a meeting is live and
   126	  suggest-local is enabled, POST a 1-token completion carrying the current system+transcript
   127	  prefix so `--cache-reuse` keeps the KV hot; click-time request then pays only the delta.
   128	
   129	### 4.5 Model manifest + runtime provisioning
   130	
   131	- `LOCAL_MODELS` manifest (in local-models.ts): id, label, HF download URL(s), sha256,
   132	  bytes, minFreeRamGB, blurb. v1 entries: `qwen3.5-0.8b` (lite — Owner's pick),
   133	  `qwen3.5-2b` (default), `qwen3.5-4b` (quality; gated to ≥ 16 GB RAM machines).
   134	  Q4_K_M instruct quants + matching mmproj. Exact URLs+sha256 pinned during R2 from
   135	  verified HF repos (prefer official Qwen; else unsloth) — fabricating checksums is
   136	  forbidden; the rock's proof includes checksum verification of a real download.
   137	- Download: HTTPS from huggingface.co with resume (Range), progress via IPC events,
   138	  sha256 streamed during download, rejected file deleted. Storage:
   139	  `app.getPath('userData')/local-llm/models/`.
   140	- Runtime: `scripts/fetch-llama-server.mjs` downloads the PINNED llama.cpp release assets
   141	  (tag + sha256 in the script) for the current build platform into `resources/llama/<platform>/`
   142	  at package time; `scripts/check-llama-sidecar.mjs` hard-fails packaging when the binary
   143	  for the target platform is missing (lesson: sherpa cross-build silently dropped
   144	  win natives). electron-builder ships it under extraResources; macOS signing includes it
   145	  (Gatekeeper-safe — a runtime downloaded at first-run would be quarantined, hence
   146	  bundle-and-sign, not download).
   147	- App size cost: ≈ 5-40 MB per platform (llama-server + dlls). Accepted.
   148	
   149	### 4.6 Settings UI (renderer)
   150	
   151	"Local AI" card in Settings (App.tsx + state.ts, following existing provider-card
   152	patterns): enable toggle; model picker with size/RAM guidance (0.8B ≈ 0.7 GB / 2B ≈ 1.4 GB /
   153	4B ≈ 2.5 GB downloads — final numbers from the pinned manifest); download button with
   154	progress + cancel; delete model; three "use for" checkboxes (Live suggestions, Summaries,
   155	Screenshots); status line (runtime running/stopped, model loaded). Renderer gets ONLY
   156	metadata via IPC (states, progress %) — never paths, port, or api-key.
   157	
   158	## 5. Error matrix
   159	
   160	| Failure | Exit/signal | Handling |
   161	|---|---|---|
   162	| Sidecar binary missing/corrupt | spawn ENOENT / sha mismatch | local ineligible; Settings shows "runtime missing — reinstall app"; audit `local.runtime.missing` |
   163	| Port bind race | llama-server exits non-zero | retry once with fresh ephemeral port |
   164	| Model checksum mismatch (download) | sha256 ≠ manifest | delete file, surface "download corrupted — retry", audit `local.model.checksum_fail` |
   165	| Model corrupt on load | server exits during load | mark model bad, prompt redownload; do NOT auto-delete without user ack |
   166	| OOM / insufficient RAM | server exit / load fail | RAM check gates download+load (os.totalmem vs minFreeRamGB); on failure suggest smaller model |
   167	| Sidecar crash mid-stream | stream aborts | onError → existing failover waterfall (cloud answers); one auto-restart per 10 min |
   168	| Health timeout (Defender first-run) | no 200 in budget | win budget 60 s; then treat as crash path |
   169	| First token > idleMs | existing watchdog (shared.ts idleWatchdog) | unchanged — failover fires |
   170	| App quit | before-quit | SIGKILL sidecar, remove temp files |
   171	
   172	## 6. Standards
   173	
   174	- Repo conventions: TypeScript strict, colocated `*.test.ts` vitest, comment style =
   175	  explain the constraint not the mechanics, `npm run typecheck` (both tsconfigs) green,
   176	  `npm test` green.
   177	- Security bar (repo's existing): renderer sandbox/contextIsolation untouched; no new
   178	  IPC that leaks paths/keys; sidecar loopback-only + api-key; downloads HTTPS +
   179	  sha256-pinned; VISION_GUARD stays on local vision turns; audit events for runtime
   180	  start/stop/crash and model download/delete.
   181	- No placeholder code, no TODO-stubs; every rock lands with its tests.
   182	
   183	## 7. Risks
   184	
   185	1. **Qwen3.5 GGUF/mmproj availability or naming differs from expectation** → R2 starts
   186	   with a verification step; if official quants are missing, fall back to unsloth quants;
   187	   if 2B mmproj is missing, default model becomes 0.8B (which the Owner already validated
   188	   exists with llama.cpp-ecosystem quants).
   189	2. **llama.cpp pinned release regressions** → pin a tag verified to load Qwen3.5 during R1;

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""R1 spike: prove pinned llama.cpp b9957 serves Qwen3.5-0.8B text+vision on this mac."""
import json, time, urllib.request, sys

BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:18181"
KEY = "spike123"
# 1x1 PNG (solid pixel) — proves the image pipeline decodes, not model IQ.
PNG_B64 = "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAADUlEQVR42mP8z8BQDwAEhQGAhKmMIQAAAABJRU5ErkJggg=="

def wait_health(budget=90):
    t0 = time.time()
    while time.time() - t0 < budget:
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(BASE + "/health", timeout=2) as r:
                if r.status == 200:
                    return time.time() - t0
        except Exception:
            time.sleep(1)
    sys.exit("health timeout")

def chat(messages, max_tokens=48):
    body = json.dumps({"model": "local", "max_tokens": max_tokens, "temperature": 0.7,
                       "top_p": 0.8, "messages": messages}).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + "/v1/chat/completions", data=body, headers={
        "Authorization": "Bearer " + KEY, "Content-Type": "application/json"})
    t0 = time.time()
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as r:
        out = json.loads(r.read())
    dt = time.time() - t0
    return dt, out["choices"][0]["message"]["content"].strip()

h = wait_health()
print(f"HEALTH ok after {h:.1f}s")

dt, txt = chat([{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in French, one short sentence."}])
print(f"TEXT {dt*1000:.0f}ms: {txt[:80]!r}")

dt, txt = chat([{"role": "user", "content": [
    {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image in five words or fewer."},
    {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64," + PNG_B64}}]}])
print(f"VISION {dt*1000:.0f}ms: {txt[:80]!r}")

prefix = ("Live transcript of the conversation I am in right now:\n" +
          ("THEM: We should review the Q3 pipeline numbers before the client call. " * 90) +
          "\n\nGive me one short thing to say next.")
dt_cold, _ = chat([{"role": "user", "content": prefix}], max_tokens=32)
print(f"PREFILL-COLD {dt_cold*1000:.0f}ms (~6k chars)")
dt_warm, txt = chat([{"role": "user", "content": prefix}], max_tokens=32)
print(f"PREFILL-WARM {dt_warm*1000:.0f}ms: {txt[:60]!r}")
print(f"SPIKE VERDICT: text+vision+cache OK; warm speedup x{dt_cold/max(dt_warm,0.001):.1f}")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""R2 spot-check: screenshot-reading quality + latency, per model. Usage: ocr-spike.py <label>"""
import base64, json, sys, time, urllib.request

BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:18181"
KEY = "spike123"
IMG = base64.b64encode(open("slide.png", "rb").read()).decode()
FACTS = ["4.2", "contoso", "q4", "friday", "10:00"]

def chat(content, max_tokens=160):
    body = json.dumps({"model": "local", "max_tokens": max_tokens, "temperature": 0.7,
                       "top_p": 0.8, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}]}).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(BASE + "/v1/chat/completions", data=body, headers={
        "Authorization": "Bearer " + KEY, "Content-Type": "application/json"})
    t0 = time.time()
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as r:
        out = json.loads(r.read())
    return time.time() - t0, out["choices"][0]["message"]["content"].strip()

t0 = time.time()
while time.time() - t0 < 120:
    try:
        if urllib.request.urlopen(BASE + "/health", timeout=2).status == 200:
            break
    except Exception:
        time.sleep(1)

label = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "model"
dt, txt = chat([
    {"type": "text", "text": "Read this slide from my meeting. List every fact on it, including numbers, names and times."},
    {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64," + IMG}}])
low = txt.lower()
hits = [f for f in FACTS if f in low]
print(f"{label} OCR {dt*1000:.0f}ms — facts {len(hits)}/{len(FACTS)} {hits}")
print("--- output ---")
print(txt)
